comparisons.peer_summary: Manufacturing depends on third-party manufacturers and foundries, yet many contracts lack long-term capacity or pricing commitments. This exposes the company to risks where suppliers may allocate capacity elsewhere, leading to unavailability of materials at reasonable prices or inability to meet demand spikes.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Micron disclose heavy reliance on external manufacturing and supply chain structures for their semiconductor operations, though the specific mechanisms differ. Intel describes its 'Smart Capital' and SCIP program as a way to access private capital to 'accelerate and scale manufacturing build-outs,' implying a strategy to fund and manage capital-intensive production expansion through strategic financial agreements. In contrast, Micron discloses that its manufacturing processes are dependent on third-party foundries and contract manufacturers, noting that many contracts lack long-term capacity or pricing commitments, which exposes Micron to risks of supply shortages. While Intel highlights the financial instrument (SCIP) used to scale its own manufacturing capabilities, Micron highlights the operational risk of depending on third-party suppliers for those manufacturing capabilities.

sentences.text: ▪SCIP. We access strategically aligned private capital to increase our flexibility and help efficiently accelerate and scale manufacturing build-outs. Our SCIP program has supported the period of accelerated manufacturing investment that commenced in early 2021. We signed our latest SCIP agreement in the second quarter of 2024 and are not contemplating further transactions in the near term.

Our manufacturing processes are also dependent on our relationships with third-party manufacturers of controllers, analog integrated circuits, and other components used in some of our products and with outsourced semiconductor foundries, assembly and test providers, contract manufacturers, logistics carriers, and other service providers, including providers of maintenance for our advanced semiconductor manufacturing equipment and providers of electricity and other utilities.

To the extent we do not have firm commitments from our third-party suppliers over a specific time period or for any specific capacity, quantity, and/or pricing, our suppliers may allocate capacity to their other customers and capacity and/or materials may not be available when needed or at reasonable prices.
